functions.name: attention_token
functions.behavior: Reads an attention marker file and returns its event token. Opens the file, reads its full contents, strips surrounding ASCII whitespace. If the stripped content is all ASCII digits (Python str.isdigit semantics), parses it as an integer token. Otherwise (empty marker, non-digit content) returns the file's st_mtime_ns (integer nanoseconds since epoch). Returns None if the file cannot be opened (missing/unreadable). This is the SHARED token accessor used by both notify_attention/_claim_attention (via the session's precomputed attention_token) and acknowledge_focused_attention (re-reading the live marker), and also by rows/assoc when building each session's attention_token at scripts/sidebar.py:492. Keep in a shared location so notify and rows agree bit-for-bit.
functions.side_effects: Read-only: opens marker file and may stat it.
edge_cases: Missing file -> None (OSError caught).
Empty legacy marker (no token content) -> st_mtime_ns, NOT None and NOT 0. This is the load-bearing legacy-format quirk: old markers carried no token, so their mtime substitutes as the event ordinal.
Non-digit content (e.g. whitespace-only, or unexpected text) -> st_mtime_ns fallback, same path as empty.
'-5' or '+5' -> Python isdigit() is False for signs, so treated as non-digit -> mtime_ns. Rust must NOT accept a leading sign as a digit token.

Unicode digits: Python str.isdigit() accepts some non-ASCII digit characters; markers are only ever ASCII from the hook, so restrict Rust to ASCII digits to avoid parsing surprises but this is effectively never exercised.
st_mtime_ns must be integer NANOSECONDS (tv_sec*1_000_000_000 + tv_nsec), matching Python os.stat().st_mtime_ns exactly — not float seconds, not millis.

functions.name: client_ttys
functions.behavior: Returns the tty path of every client attached to this sidebar's own tmux session — the terminals a desktop notification is written to. Runs `tmux display-message -p -t <SIDEBAR_PANE> '#{session_name}'` and strips the result; if empty, returns an empty vec. Otherwise runs `tmux list-clients -t <session> -F '#{client_tty}'`, splits stdout on '\n', and keeps every line whose trimmed form is non-empty.
functions.side_effects: Two tmux subprocess invocations (read-only tmux queries).
edge_cases: Empty/blank session name (tmux failure or detached) -> return [] without calling list-clients.
No clients attached -> list-clients yields nothing -> [].

Filter predicate is `line.strip() truthy` but the RETAINED value is the ORIGINAL, unstripped line. In practice client_tty is a clean /dev/pts path with no surrounding whitespace, so trailing-whitespace preservation is moot; still, replicate: filter on trimmed-nonempty, push the raw line.
Multiple clients -> multiple ttys, one OSC write each per firing (see notify_attention).
Split on '\n' only (not on other line endings); a trailing newline produces a final empty element that the filter drops.

functions.name: claim_attention
functions.signature: fn claim_attention(notified_dir: &Path, session_id: &str, token: i64) -> bool
functions.behavior: Atomically claims a NEWER attention event across every per-window sidebar process, so exactly one sidebar fires each event. Ensures NOTIFIED dir exists. Path = notified_dir/session_id. Records whether the flag file already EXISTED (checked BEFORE the open). Opens the flag O_CREAT|O_RDWR|append ('a+' equivalent), takes a BLOCKING exclusive fcntl advisory lock (flock LOCK_EX) held for the whole read-modify-write. Seeks to 0, reads current contents, strips. Computes previous_token: if the stripped previous is all digits -> int(previous); else if the file EXISTED before this open -> fstat(fd).st_mtime_ns; else 0. If token <= previous_token -> return false (already fired this event or a newer one). Otherwise seek 0, truncate, write the decimal token, flush, return true. Lock releases when the handle closes.
functions.side_effects: Creates NOTIFIED dir and per-session flag file; overwrites flag contents with the winning token; holds a cross-process exclusive advisory lock during the critical section.
edge_cases: token <= previous_token returns false — the `<=` makes it exactly-once PER TOKEN VALUE: a repeat of the same token never re-fires, but a strictly greater token does (this is why consecutive attention events on an already-focused pane still each fire once).
Freshly created flag (did not exist before open): 'a+' creates it, contents empty/non-digit, existed=false -> previous_token=0, so any positive token wins first fire.
Legacy/empty EXISTING flag (non-digit contents): previous_token = fstat(fd).st_mtime_ns — uses the OPEN FD's stat (fstat), not a path stat, deliberately. Rust must fstat the same handle.
existed must be sampled BEFORE opening, because opening with O_CREAT would otherwise make the file 'exist'; this distinguishes a first-ever claim (->0) from a legacy empty flag (->mtime).
flock is BLOCKING (LOCK_EX). Do not use try_lock; a sidebar must wait so claims serialize. Advisory POSIX flock — matches Python fcntl.flock.
Any OSError (mkdir/open/lock/io) -> return false (do not fire). Fail-closed.

Mixed token domains: tokens may be small monotonic integers written by the hook OR large mtime_ns integers (legacy markers). Comparisons are plain integer <=; both fit i64. A legacy mtime_ns previous vs a small-int new token would make the new token look 'older' and be suppressed — inherited from Python, preserve as-is.
truncate then write ensures no stale trailing bytes from a longer prior token remain.

functions.name: acknowledge_focused_attention
functions.behavior: Clears a session's attention marker (and its in-memory dot) ONLY after its signal has already been given, and only when a pane showing it is focused. Builds a map sid -> token from every session whose attention_token is Some AND whose pane is in focused_panes (later placements of the same id overwrite, but all placements share one marker so the token is identical). For each (sid, token): re-reads the LIVE marker via attention_token(ATTENTION/sid); if it differs from token, skip (a newer attention event arrived since fetch — do not clear it). Otherwise unlink the marker; on failure, skip (leave the dot). On success, recompute status = 'working' if WORKING/sid exists else '' , then for every in-memory session with matching id AND matching attention_token, set attention_token=None and status=that value.
functions.side_effects: Deletes the attention marker file; mutates the in-memory sessions slice (clears attention_token, resets status). Reads the WORKING marker's existence.
edge_cases: attention_token None -> session skipped when building the focused map.
Marker-token mismatch on re-read (new event since fetch) -> continue, do NOT unlink, do NOT clear the dot — this is the race guard that prevents acknowledging an event that was never signalled.

unlink OSError (already removed by another sidebar) -> continue WITHOUT mutating sessions; the in-memory dot stays until the next poll observes the marker gone. Matches Python: mutation only happens after a successful unlink.
Post-clear status is recomputed from the WORKING marker because attention/working are mutually exclusive on disk but the turn may have resumed working; do not blindly set ''.
In-memory mutation is gated on `attention_token == token` as well as id, guarding the (degenerate) case where placements diverged; preserve the double guard.
Must run AFTER notify_attention in the same tick (main calls notify then acknowledge): signalling reads the marker/token, acknowledgement then clears it. Reversing the order would drop signals.
Iteration order of the focused map only affects unlink ordering, not correctness; a plain HashMap is fine here (unlike notify_attention's ordered fire).

functions.name: notify_attention
functions.signature: fn notify_attention(sessions: &[Session], bell_on: bool, osc_mode: OscMode, tmux: &Tmux, paths: &StatePaths, sidebar_pane: &str)  // OscMode = Off | Osc777 | Osc9
functions.behavior: Rings the terminal bell and/or raises a desktop notification exactly once per NEW attention event, fired from the poll loop (so nothing signals while the sidebar is off, and signals precede focus-acknowledgement because the target terminal may be backgrounded). Step 1 pick one representative placement per session id: iterate sessions; skip attention_token==None; for each id keep the first seen, but UPGRADE to a placement whose window.active is true when the current representative's window is not active (so the notification is titled by the active window's name). Step 2, only if bell_on || osc_mode != Off: for each (sid, session) in insertion order, call claim_attention(NOTIFIED, sid, token); if it loses (false) skip. If osc_mode != Off: win = session.window.name; text = if label non-empty then format!("{win} \u{00B7} {label}") else win (middle dot U+00B7, space-padded); for Osc777 esc = "\x1b]777;notify;{agent};{text}\x07"; for Osc9 esc = "\x1b]9;{text}\x07"; write esc to EVERY client tty (client_ttys re-queried per firing session). If bell_on && session.pane non-empty: resolve the pane tty via `tmux display-message -p -t <pane> '#{pane_tty}'` (stripped) and write a BEL byte (0x07) to it. Step 3 (ALWAYS, regardless of bell/osc): garbage-collect NOTIFIED flags — list the dir (errors -> empty), and for each flag whose session id has NO surviving REGISTRY file, unlink it once its mtime is at least 5 seconds old (grace longer than any in-flight poll); ignore errors.
functions.side_effects: Locks/writes per-session dedup flags (via claim_attention); writes BEL bytes to pane ttys; writes OSC escape sequences to client ttys; runs tmux subprocesses (pane_tty lookup, and client_ttys' two queries per firing); deletes retired flag files after the grace period.
edge_cases: Representative selection prefers the ACTIVE-window placement but only ever upgrades once (there is at most one active window); otherwise first-seen wins. Not last-seen, not last-active.
claim_attention is called ONLY inside the `bell_on || osc_mode` guard — flags are written only when signalling is enabled; a config with both off writes no flags (but GC still runs).
Claiming ties bell and OSC together: winning the claim then fires BOTH enabled channels for that event. A single token is consumed per event across both channels.
Bell fires only when session.pane is non-empty (a real pane tty exists). OSC fires even for pane-less/daemon-hosted sessions (label may be empty -> text is just the window name).
OscMode mapping mirrors osc_notify_mode(): '777'/'on'/'1'/'yes'/'true' -> Osc777; '9' -> Osc9; everything else -> Off. Off is falsy in the `or` guard.

client_ttys() is re-invoked for each firing session (N tmux round-trips for N events) rather than cached — preserve or document if optimizing; behaviorally identical only if the client set is stable within the tick.

GC keeps a flag while REGISTRY/<id> exists (session alive) so its latest token survives and a stale poll cannot reclaim an older event after focus clears the marker; only retired sessions' flags are eligible, and only after >=5s (time.time()-getmtime >= 5).
Escape bytes: ESC=0x1b, BEL=0x07; the separator is U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT encoded UTF-8 (0xC2 0xB7), surrounded by single spaces.
session.agent (agent type, e.g. 'claude'/'copilot') is embedded verbatim as the OSC 777 notify title field.
All tty/subprocess writes are best-effort: failures are swallowed and must never disturb the draw loop.

functions.name: write_tty
functions.behavior: Best-effort raw write of bytes to a tty device path (a pane tty for the bell, a client tty for the OSC notification). No-op if path is empty. Opens the path for writing and writes data; any OSError is swallowed. Never disturbs the draw loop. Support helper for notify_attention.
functions.side_effects: Opens and writes to a tty device file.
edge_cases: Empty path -> immediate no-op (bell path is derived from a possibly-empty pane_tty lookup).
Open/write failure (tty gone, permission) -> silently ignored.
Python opens in text mode and writes a str; Rust should open in a mode that writes the exact bytes (the OSC/BEL sequences) without newline translation.

parity_risks: TOKEN DOMAIN MIXING: tokens are either small monotonic ints (hook-written) or large st_mtime_ns ints (legacy/empty markers). All comparisons are plain integer <= in both claim_attention and acknowledge. Use i64 everywhere; do not normalize or coerce. A legacy mtime_ns previous can suppress a small-int new token — this quirk is inherited and must be preserved.

st_mtime_ns must be exact integer nanoseconds (tv_sec*1e9+tv_nsec), matching Python os.stat().st_mtime_ns / os.fstat().st_mtime_ns. Any float-seconds or millisecond approximation breaks dedup ordering for legacy markers.

claim_attention uses <= (not <): exactly-once per token VALUE. Re-firing the same event must be impossible; a strictly greater token must still win. Off-by-one here silently drops or duplicates notifications.

'existed' in claim_attention is sampled BEFORE the O_CREAT open; getting this wrong makes a first-ever claim look like a legacy empty flag (mtime instead of 0) and can suppress the very first notification.
flock must be BLOCKING exclusive (LOCK_EX), advisory POSIX flock, held across the read-modify-write. A non-blocking or dropped lock lets multiple per-window sidebars double-fire the same event.
acknowledge re-reads the LIVE marker token and skips on mismatch — the race guard against clearing an unsignalled newer event. Must re-stat/re-read, not trust the cached session token.

ORDERING: notify_attention's representative map and fire loop rely on INSERTION order (Python dict). Use an insertion-ordered map (e.g. IndexMap) so the representative-upgrade rule and per-event fire order are deterministic. acknowledge's map order is irrelevant.
Representative selection is first-seen-then-upgrade-to-active, NOT max-by-anything; replicate the exact conditional (`cur is None or (s.window.active and not cur.window.active)`).
Call order in the glue loop is fixed: notify_attention THEN acknowledge_focused_attention (sidebar.py:1083-1084). Signalling must precede marker clearing.

GC grace is `now - getmtime(flag) >= 5` seconds and is gated on absence of REGISTRY/<id>. Both conditions are load-bearing: dropping the registry check would let a live session's latest-token flag be reclaimed by a stale poll after focus clears the marker.
OSC separator is U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT (UTF-8 0xC2 0xB7) with surrounding spaces; ESC=0x1b, BEL=0x07 terminators. Byte-exact strings matter for terminals parsing OSC 777/9.
bell fires only when session.pane is non-empty; OSC fires regardless of pane (daemon-hosted sessions). Empty label collapses the OSC text to just the window name (no separator).
claim_attention is invoked only under `bell_on || osc_mode` — flags are not written when signalling is disabled, yet GC always runs. Preserve this asymmetry.
attention_token treats empty/non-digit markers as mtime_ns (legacy back-compat), and Python str.isdigit() rejects signs; restrict the Rust digit test to plain ASCII digits with no sign.
All tty writes and tmux calls are best-effort and must swallow errors; propagating an error out of the poll loop is a parity break (would kill the sidebar).
client_ttys retains the raw (unstripped) line while filtering on the trimmed value; and _client_ttys is re-queried per firing session, not cached.
